newsitem.title: USA: Commerce's Price says US economic outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Commerce's Price says US economic outlook positive.

text.p: A Commerce Department economist on Thursday called the near-term U.S. economic outlook positive, with retail sales rising and exports continuing to grow at a healthy pace.
"The near-term outlook for the economy remains positive," Acting Commerce Undersecretary Lee Price told reporters.

The Commerce Department reported earlier that economic growth slowed markedly in the second quarter, to a 2.2 percent annualized pace from 4.9 percent in the first quarter, as consumers cut their spending sharply.

However, Price said that consumer spending seems to be bouncing back. "The June upturn in retail sales suggests consumer spending is returning to a favorable trend rate of growth," he said, noting consumer confidence remains strong.
Home building also looks set to enjoy further modest growth in the current quarter, while inventories do not seem out of line with sales, he added.
Price said he expects U.S. exports to continue to expand at a healthy pace, thanks to what he called a "generally favorable" economic outlook for overseas economies.
He saw few imbalances in the economy, with little upward pressure evident on prices of crude and intermediate goods.

"Because capacity is now expanding at a four percent pace compared with just two percent pace in 1993, output can now grow at twice the pace today that it could in 1993 without increasing pressures on capacity," Price said.
